Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. - **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

+# Note: n_0979_870a

+curl's internal `--retry N` does NOT resume with `-C -`: on a timed-out attempt it starts over from offset 0, truncating the partial output (verified locally against a throttling range server — transfer restarted at 0 with `--retry 2 -C - --max-time 2`). 1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:

   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. Actually the comment overestimates, which is safe. 730s < 900s leaves 170s for unzip. unzip of 92.7MB zip — fast, seconds. OK.

But wait — the reserve used in the test is 60s ("one connect timeout + unzip + slack"), while the comment says 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s. 730 + 60 = 790 ≤ 900. Consistent.

**Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

**Issue K: `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — shared /tmp on self-hosted runner.** Two matrix jobs (arm64 + x86_64) build on ONE self-hosted runner (per the comment about per-arch keychains: "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner"). Old code: both jobs write to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` too. If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

The ticket says both "Build macOS x86_64" and "Build macOS arm64" failed in the same leg run. Yes — that means both jobs run at the same time on the same machine. So `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` is a shared mutable file between two concurrent jobs:
- Job A: `rm -f` the zip while Job B is mid-resume → Job B's next curl attempt with `-C -` sees missing file → restarts from 0 (acceptable-ish)

Actually curl -o opens with O_CREAT|O_WRONLY... without -C, it truncates? No — curl -o overwrites from the start (truncates at open, then writes from offset 0…

Contradictory evidence. Maybe the runner normally serializes (1 job slot), but overlapping runs (daily + manual dispatch) can put two jobs of DIFFERENT runs on... no, a single runner processes one job at a time regardless of run. Unless there are TWO runner processes registered on the same machine (common for self-hosted to parallelize). The keychain race evidence suggests two runner processes existed at some point.

Actually — wait. Even without `rm -f`, the OLD code had both jobs writing to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` concurrently (curl -o truncates and writes; two writers → garbage). This is actually more relevant now: the whole point of the loop is retries on failure, but HTTP-level failures (404, 502, 503 from GitHub) return exit 0 and bypass the retry logic entirely. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. - **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

+# Note: n_0979_870a

+curl's internal `--retry N` does NOT resume with `-C -`: on a timed-out attempt it starts over from offset 0, truncating the partial output (verified locally against a throttling range server — transfer restarted at 0 with `--retry 2 -C - --max-time 2`). 1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:

   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. Actually the comment overestimates, which is safe. 730s < 900s leaves 170s for unzip. unzip of 92.7MB zip — fast, seconds. OK.

But wait — the reserve used in the test is 60s ("one connect timeout + unzip + slack"), while the comment says 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s. 730 + 60 = 790 ≤ 900. Consistent.

**Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

**Issue K: `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — shared /tmp on self-hosted runner.** Two matrix jobs (arm64 + x86_64) build on ONE self-hosted runner (per the comment about per-arch keychains: "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner"). Old code: both jobs write to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` too. If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

The ticket says both "Build macOS x86_64" and "Build macOS arm64" failed in the same leg run. Yes — that means both jobs run at the same time on the same machine. So `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` is a shared mutable file between two concurrent jobs:
- Job A: `rm -f` the zip while Job B is mid-resume → Job B's next curl attempt with `-C -` sees missing file → restarts from 0 (acceptable-ish)

Actually curl -o opens with O_CREAT|O_WRONLY... without -C, it truncates? No — curl -o overwrites from the start (truncates at open, then writes from offset 0…

This comment says the two matrix jobs both ran one self-hosted runner AND raced — implying concurrency happened in practice. But the build-macos-cli comment says the self-hosted matrix "serializes". Contradictory evidence. Maybe the runner normally serializes (1 job slot), but overlapping runs (daily + manual dispatch) can put two jobs of DIFFERENT runs on... no, a single runner processes one job at a time regardless of run. Unless there are TWO runner processes registered on the same machine (common for self-hosted to parallelize). The keychain race evidence suggests two runner processes existed at some point.

The workflow comment at line ~361 (keychain) explicitly says "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)" — that's direct evidence of parallel execution in practice (builds 86). Actually — wait. Even without `rm -f`, the OLD code had both jobs writing to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` concurrently (curl -o truncates and writes; two writers → garbage). So the download corruption race predates this PR. BUT the old code ALSO had no `rm -f` — and the old failure mode was masked by the always-timeout bug. Now that downloads can actually succeed, the race becomes REACHABLE (before, the step never got past attempt 1 anyway). So the PR makes the latent race live. IMPORTANT is fair. This is actually more relevant now: the whole point of the loop is retries on failure, but HTTP-level failures (404, 502, 503 from GitHub) return exit 0 and bypass the retry logic entirely. Old code: same gap (--retry-all-errors didn't help because no HTTP failure exit without --fail). This is a genuine SUGGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. - **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

+# Note: n_0979_870a

+curl's internal `--retry N` does NOT resume with `-C -`: on a timed-out attempt it starts over from offset 0, truncating the partial output (verified locally against a throttling range server — transfer restarted at 0 with `--retry 2 -C - --max-time 2`). 1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:

   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. Actually the comment overestimates, which is safe. 730s < 900s leaves 170s for unzip. unzip of 92.7MB zip — fast, seconds. OK.

But wait — the reserve used in the test is 60s ("one connect timeout + unzip + slack"), while the comment says 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s. 730 + 60 = 790 ≤ 900. Consistent.

**Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

**Issue K: `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — shared /tmp on self-hosted runner.** Two matrix jobs (arm64 + x86_64) build on ONE self-hosted runner (per the comment about per-arch keychains: "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner"). Old code: both jobs write to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` too. If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

The ticket says both "Build macOS x86_64" and "Build macOS arm64" failed in the same leg run. Yes — that means both jobs run at the same time on the same machine. So `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` is a shared mutable file between two concurrent jobs:
- Job A: `rm -f` the zip while Job B is mid-resume → Job B's next curl attempt with `-C -` sees missing file → restarts from 0 (acceptable-ish)

Actually curl -o opens with O_CREAT|O_WRONLY... without -C, it truncates? No — curl -o overwrites from the start (truncates at open, then writes from offset 0…

But then how did the keychain race happen ("both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner; a shared build.keychain raced")? This comment says the two matrix jobs both ran one self-hosted runner AND raced — implying concurrency happened in practice. But the build-macos-cli comment says the self-hosted matrix "serializes". Contradictory evidence. Maybe the runner normally serializes (1 job slot), but overlapping runs (daily + manual dispatch) can put two jobs of DIFFERENT runs on... no, a single runner processes one job at a time regardless of run. Unless there are TWO runner processes registered on the same machine (common for self-hosted to parallelize). The keychain race evidence suggests two runner processes existed at some point. 

Also the failed daily run: BOTH x86_64 and arm64 legs failed at the same step with the same timeout — from the log, arm64 was downloading 07:12-07:15. Were both downloading simultaneously? The workflow comment at line ~361 (keychain) explicitly says "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)" — that's direct evidence of parallel execution in practice (builds 86). Actually — wait. Even without `rm -f`, the OLD code had both jobs writing to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` concurrently (curl -o truncates and writes; two writers → garbage). So the download corruption race predates this PR. BUT the old code ALSO had no `rm -f` — and the old failure mode was masked by the always-timeout bug. Now that downloads can actually succeed, the race becomes REACHABLE (before, the step never got past attempt 1 anyway). So the PR makes the latent race live. IMPORTANT is fair. This is actually more relevant now: the whole point of the loop is retries on failure, but HTTP-level failures (404, 502, 503 from GitHub) return exit 0 and bypass the retry logic entirely. Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"

            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts

            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip

Now let me analyze the change carefully. Key observations:

1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:

   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. Actually the comment overestimates, which is safe. 730s < 900s leaves 170s for unzip. unzip of 92.7MB zip — fast, seconds. OK.

But wait — the reserve used in the test is 60s ("one connect timeout + unzip + slack"), while the comment says 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s. 730 + 60 = 790 ≤ 900. Consistent.

**Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

**Issue K: `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — shared /tmp on self-hosted runner.** Two matrix jobs (arm64 + x86_64) build on ONE self-hosted runner (per the comment about per-arch keychains: "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner"). Both jobs could run concurrently and both download to `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — RACE CONDITION! Wait, was this a pre-existing issue? Old code: both jobs write to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` too. If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

The ticket says both "Build macOS x86_64" and "Build macOS arm64" failed in the same leg run. Yes — that means both jobs run at the same time on the same machine. So `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` is a shared mutable file between two concurrent jobs:
- Job A: `rm -f` the zip while Job B is mid-resume → Job B's next curl attempt with `-C -` sees missing file → restarts from 0 (acceptable-ish)

Actually curl -o opens with O_CREAT|O_WRONLY... without -C, it truncates? No — curl -o overwrites from the start (truncates at open, then writes from offset 0…

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. **Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

**Issue K: `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — shared /tmp on self-hosted runner.** Two matrix jobs (arm64 + x86_64) build on ONE self-hosted runner (per the comment about per-arch keychains: "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner"). If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz"
          tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # Ensure the release exists (race-safe with release-macos). Title
          # is the bare tag vX.Y.Z (issue #282: one naming scheme, no
          # "Fa " prefixes), latest is explicit.
          if ! gh release view "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "$RELEASE_TAG" \
              --title "$RELEASE_TAG" \
              --generate-notes \
              --latest \
              --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
          fi
          gh release upload "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

  build-extension:
    name: Build Chrome extension
    needs: version

    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

+# Note: n_0979_870a
+

Now let me analyze the change carefully. Key observations:

1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:
   - Old: `curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 -o /tmp/... URL`
   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? - **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
