# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). {"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +349
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T11:04:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
            # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
            # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
            # let one job's rm -f unlink the other's in-flight partial, then
            # both curls interleave bytes into one path.
            ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
            rm -f "$ZIP"
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do

              # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error

                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                exit 1

              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."

            # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern

            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

            # --retry-all-errors retries them (sha256 below guards corruption)
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz \

        with:
          path: flutter_app/macos/Pods

          mkdir -p lib/core/services

            '// ignore_for_file: constant_identifier_names' \

        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"

          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.

          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"

            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts

            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do

                -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \

              sleep 5

1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:

   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. Actually the comment overestimates, which is safe. 730s < 900s leaves 170s for unzip. unzip of 92.7MB zip — fast, seconds. OK.

But wait — the reserve used in the test is 60s ("one connect timeout + unzip + slack"), while the comment says 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s. 730 + 60 = 790 ≤ 900. Consistent.

**Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

**Issue K: `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — shared /tmp on self-hosted runner.** Two matrix jobs (arm64 + x86_64) build on ONE self-hosted runner (per the comment about per-arch keychains: "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner"). Both jobs could run concurrently and both download to `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — RACE CONDITION! Wait, was this a pre-existing issue? Old code: both jobs write to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` too. If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

The ticket says both "Build macOS x86_64" and "Build macOS arm64" failed in the same leg run. Yes — that means both jobs run at the same time on the same machine. So `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` is a shared mutable file between two concurrent jobs:

Before this change, both jobs also wrote to the same path concurrently (interleaved -o writes). So the race is pre-existing. Actually curl -o opens with O_CREAT|O_WRONLY... without -C, it truncates? No — curl -o overwrites from the start (truncates at open, then writes from offset 0…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +349
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T11:04:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
            # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
            # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
            # let one job's rm -f unlink the other's in-flight partial, then
            # both curls interleave bytes into one path.
            ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
            rm -f "$ZIP"

              # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error

              if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \

                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                exit 1

              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."

            # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern

            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

Now let me analyze the change carefully. Key observations:

1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:
   - Old: `curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 -o /tmp/... URL`
   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. Actually the comment overestimates, which is safe. 730s < 900s leaves 170s for unzip. unzip of 92.7MB zip — fast, seconds. OK.

But wait — the reserve used in the test is 60s ("one connect timeout + unzip + slack"), while the comment says 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s. 730 + 60 = 790 ≤ 900. Consistent.

**Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

**Issue K: `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — shared /tmp on self-hosted runner.** Two matrix jobs (arm64 + x86_64) build on ONE self-hosted runner (per the comment about per-arch keychains: "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner"). Both jobs could run concurrently and both download to `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` — RACE CONDITION! Wait, was this a pre-existing issue? Old code: both jobs write to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` too. If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

The ticket says both "Build macOS x86_64" and "Build macOS arm64" failed in the same leg run. The comment in the workflow says "both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". Yes — that means both jobs run at the same time on the same machine. So `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` is a shared mutable file between two concurrent jobs:
- Job A: `rm -f` the zip while Job B is mid-resume → Job B's next curl attempt with `-C -` sees missing file → restarts from 0 (acceptable-ish)

RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz"
          tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # Ensure the release exists (race-safe with release-macos). Title
          # is the bare tag vX.Y.Z (issue #282: one naming scheme, no
          # "Fa " prefixes), latest is explicit.
          if ! gh release view "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "$RELEASE_TAG" \
              --title "$RELEASE_TAG" \
              --generate-notes \
              --latest \
              --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true
          fi
          gh release upload "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset" --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

  build-extension:
    name: Build Chrome extension
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +349
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T11:04:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

`build-macos` runs `arm64` and `x86_64` on **one self-hosted runner**, and this same file documents (line 361) that these two jobs have already raced on shared runner state — "a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create emptied it under the other's codesign)". In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash

```

Wait — there's a subtle issue in the new test:

```dart
expect(
  run,
  contains('echo "$digest  \$ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'),
  ...
);
```

In Dart, `'echo "$digest  \$ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -'` — this is a non-raw string with `$digest` INTERPOLATED (the Dart variable digest) and `\$ZIP` escaped to literal `$ZIP`. So the expected string is `echo "aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -`. The workflow line is `echo "aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -`. Matches. ✓

Now the ordering assertions:
```dart
final doneIndex = run.indexOf(RegExp(r'^\s*done$', multiLine: true));
final checkIndex = run.indexOf('shasum -a 256 -c -');
final unzipIndex = run.indexOf(r'unzip -q "$ZIP"');
```
- `doneIndex` — first `done` line in the step's run. The step run at line 311-375ish: `set -euo pipefail`, if/elif/else with the for loop inside the else branch... `done` closes the for loop. First match should be that `done` (line ~364). OK.
- `checkIndex` — first `shasum -a 256 -c -` in the run. Wait — the step's run block: does it contain another shasum? No, that's the GEMMA step (a different step). This step's run has only the one shasum. But wait — `run.indexOf('shasum -a 256 -c -')` — the echo line contains it. ✓ checkIndex > doneIndex ✓ (shasum comes after the loop).
- `unzipIndex` — first `unzip -q "$ZIP"` — after checkIndex ✓.

Hmm, but these `indexOf` checks are positional across the whole run string — they verify order but the assertions use `greaterThan`. Fine.

Now — CRITICAL verification: the pinned sha256 digest `aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98` for `https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. That's the new failure mode introduced: if the digest is wrong, the step goes from "timeout at 15min" to "sha256 mismatch fail after ~310s download" — still red. key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
            # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
            # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
            # let one job's rm -f unlink the other's in-flight partial, then
            # both curls interleave bytes into one path.
            ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
            rm -f "$ZIP"
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
              # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
              # engages this loop's retries and the explicit failure below.
              if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                -o "$ZIP" \
                https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
              sleep 5
            done
            # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
            # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
            # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
            # as the litertlm download above).
            echo "aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -

- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

+title: "curl's internal `--retry N` does NOT resume with `-C -`: on a timed-out attempt it starts over from offset 0, truncating the partial output (verified locally against a throttling range server — transfer restarted at 0 with `--retry 2 -C - --max-time 2`). +# Note: n_0979_870a
+
+curl's internal `--retry N` does NOT resume with `-C -`: on a timed-out attempt it starts over from offset 0, truncating the partial output (verified locally against a throttling range server — transfer restarted at 0 with `--retry 2 -C - --max-time 2`). The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

- **Additions**: +349
- **Deletions**: -7

- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T11:04:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
            # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
            # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
            # let one job's rm -f unlink the other's in-flight partial, then
            # both curls interleave bytes into one path.
            ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
            rm -f "$ZIP"
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
              # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
              # engages this loop's retries and the explicit failure below.
              if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                -o "$ZIP" \
                https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
              sleep 5
            done
            # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
            # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
            # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern
            # as the litertlm download above).
            echo "aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +233
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T10:15:29Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. The 416 case can only happen if the file size == remote size but the last attempt exited non-zero — rare edge (e.g. --max-time fires exactly when last bytes flushed but curl hadn't finished closing). Then attempt 2 gets 416 and exits 33... and after 3 attempts, step fails. Rare edge, worth a SUGGESTION maybe? Actually there's `--fail` considerations too.

**Issue F: no `--fail` flag.** The old curl also didn't have `--fail`. Without `--fail`, curl returns exit 0 even on HTTP errors like 404/500 (as long as it got a response body). So if the release asset is gone (404 HTML page), curl "succeeds", writes the HTML error page to the zip, then `unzip` fails. That was true of the old code too (not a regression). But wait — with `-C -` this becomes more interesting: 404 responses... not really changed. Hmm, actually this is a pre-existing issue. Not a regression but the review could mention as SUGGESTION: add `--fail --retry-all-errors`... but they removed `--retry-all-errors` deliberately. `--fail` would make curl exit 22 on HTTP >= 400 — a real improvement worth suggesting since now the download success feeds directly to unzip. Actually wait, with `-C -` + `--fail` + 404, the exit code would be 22, loop retries, eventually fails with a clear message. This is a legit suggestion but pre-existing behavior (old code also lacked --fail). The PR description says "retries moved to an explicit bash loop"; adding --fail would be a natural part of this change. I'd rate SUGGESTION.

**Issue G: `set -euo pipefail` with the loop** — `if curl ...; then break; fi` — curl failing inside `if` condition doesn't trigger `set -e`. Good. `sleep 5` fine. The loop's final `done`, then `unzip`. If all 3 attempts fail, `exit 1` explicitly. Good.

Wait, actually there's a subtle `set -e` interaction: `if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` — fine.

**Issue H: budget arithmetic**. 3 attempts × 240s = 720s + 2 sleeps × 5s = 730s. Plus `--connect-timeout 30` — is connect timeout inside max-time? Yes, `--max-time` caps the ENTIRE operation including connect, so worst case per attempt is 240s total, not 240 + 30. The comment says "3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s" — that's slightly double-counting connect (max-time includes connect time), making the estimate conservative. Actually the comment overestimates, which is safe. 730s < 900s leaves 170s for unzip. unzip of 92.7MB zip — fast, seconds. OK.

But wait — the reserve used in the test is 60s ("one connect timeout + unzip + slack"), while the comment says 30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s. 730 + 60 = 790 ≤ 900. Consistent.

**Issue I: does the loop risk blowing the step timeout in the unzip?** unzip is after loop, within the same 15-min step. Worst case download 730s + unzip few seconds + connect... fine.

**Issue J: What about the FIRST attempt succeeding part-way and second attempt resuming?** `-C -` resumes. Good.

Old code: both jobs write to the same `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` too. If both jobs run concurrently on the same runner (GitHub runs matrix jobs concurrently — but on a self-hosted runner with 1 job slot they'd be serialized; if the runner has multiple job slots / multiple runner processes, they can run in parallel).

Yes — that means both jobs run at the same time on the same machine. So `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` is a shared mutable file between two concurrent jobs:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1154
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1154
- **Title**: gh-1149 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1149` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +349
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-01T10:14:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T11:04:55Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-01):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (per-runner, keyed by the release tag) —
          #    every slot is first-run-warm forever;
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the 15-min
          #    step cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): --retry N is N
          #    retries ON TOP OF the initial attempt, so worst case is
          #    (N+1) × max-time + N × retry-delay. 3 × 240s + 2 × 5s + one
          #    30s connect + unzip ≈ 790s < 900s. The old "3 retries × 240s"
          #    math forgot the initial attempt (975s > 900s → the step
          #    timeout fired mid-retry), and without -C - no 240s attempt
          #    could ever deliver the 92.7MB asset at this link's ~300KB/s
          #    (it needs ~309s) — every attempt died at the cap having
          #    restarted from byte 0.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # -C - makes each loop attempt RESUME the partial zip (Range
            # requests), so slow links make forward progress; retries live
            # in THIS loop (not curl --retry, which would add extra attempts
            # AND restart+truncate instead of resuming). Budget: 3 × 240s
            # max-time + 2 × 5s sleeps = 730s < the 15-min step cap, leaving
            # connect + unzip + slack (gh-1149).
            # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
            # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
            # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
            # let one job's rm -f unlink the other's in-flight partial, then
            # both curls interleave bytes into one path.
            ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
            rm -f "$ZIP"
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
              # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
              # engages this loop's retries and the explicit failure below.
              if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \

                break

              if [ "$attempt" = "3" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework download failed after $attempt attempts" >&2
                exit 1

              echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."

            # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache (same pattern

            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **8465 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures** (env-dependent skips only).

### Notes

- The step failure also blocked the actions/cache warm-up; the first green run after this fix repopulates `wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0` and later runs take the cache-hit fast path.
- Latent, untouched (out of scope): ci.yml ×2 / nightly.yml / build-mobile.yml share the same `--retry 3 --max-time 600` off-by-one, but complete attempt 1 on their faster links; `timeout-minutes: 15` and the #351 budget arithmetic are unchanged.

Now let me analyze the change carefully. Key observations:

1. **The curl loop change** in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`:
   - Old: `curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 -o /tmp/... URL`
   - New: bash loop with 3 attempts, each `curl -L -C --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240`, `rm -f` before loop, sleep 5 between attempts, exit 1 after 3rd failure.

Let me check some critical things:

**Issue A: integrity check.** The old code and new code both download a zip and then `unzip -q`. Does the workflow verify the sha256 of the WasmRun.xcframework.zip? Let me check. The companion dylib step (litertlm) has a `shasum -a 256 -c -` check. The WasmRun download does not appear to have a sha256 check in what I've seen. With `-C -` resume, a corrupted/stale partial file risk is real: if the server returns different content ranges or the partial file gets corrupted, `-C -` will blindly append. The `unzip` will catch zip corruption in most cases (CRC check), so `unzip -q` failing would fail the step. Actually unzip does verify CRC32 per-file, so corruption would be caught. Not a blocker but worth noting? The old code had the same lack of sha256 check. Hmm, but with resume, byte-level mismatch (e.g. asset re-uploaded with different content mid-download) could silently produce a corrupt zip — unzip CRC would catch it. Let me check if there's a sha256 verification step for this asset elsewhere.

**Issue B: `curl` exit code handling with `-C -` and `--max-time`**. When curl is killed by `--max-time`, exit code 28. The loop handles non-zero by sleeping and retrying. Fine.

**Issue C: partial file handling when curl fails with exit code != 0 but leaves no file** — `-C -` with no existing file just starts from 0. Fine.

**Issue D: `-C -` with a server that doesn't support Range requests.** GitHub release assets redirect to a signed S3/objects URL which supports ranges. Fine. But note: curl with `-C -` and `-L`: when following a redirect, curl applies the range to the redirected request too. Fine.

**Issue E (IMPORTANT): `-C -` semantics with `-o` when file exists and server returns 416** — if the partial file is already complete (all bytes downloaded) but curl reported failure last time (e.g., timeout hit at exactly the end), the next attempt requests Range: bytes=<size>- and the server returns 416 (Range Not Satisfiable). curl treats 416 as an error (exit 33 unless `--fail` handling...). Actually curl exit code 33 is "HTTP range error". Hmm — but there's a subtlety: if the file is fully downloaded, the previous curl would have returned success (exit 0), broken out of the loop. In exactly the gh-1149 cold-cache scenario both arch jobs reach this download branch concurrently and now share one fixed path:

```

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: add `--fail` — the retry loop never engages on HTTP errors**

The loop retries only when curl exits non-zero, but without `--fail` curl exits **0** on HTTP ≥ 400 (404 / 502 / 503 from GitHub are the most common transient failures) and happily writes the error page into `/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip`. Result: no retry, and `unzip` then fails with a misleading "not a zip" error instead of the loop's clear "download failed after 3 attempts".

The old `--retry-all-errors` had the same gap (HTTP errors aren't curl errors without `--fail`), but this loop is explicitly designed to own retries — make it actually own them:

```bash
if curl -fL -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
```

Safe with this design: a genuine 404 makes all 3 attempts exit 22 quickly, and the step fails with the explicit message at line 351. (`-fsSL` is already the convention elsewhere in this repo, e.g. daily-publish.yml.)
"}

## PR Description

### Root Cause

The daily `cli` leg failed in `build-macos.yml` → "Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework": the self-hosted runner downloads the pinned 92.7 MB upstream asset at ~300 KB/s (needs ~309 s, ETA `0:05:09` in the log), but every curl attempt was capped at `--max-time 240` **with no resume flag**, so no attempt could ever finish. On top of that, `--retry 3` means 3 retries *on top of* the initial attempt → 4 attempts × 240 s + 3 × 5 s = **975 s > the step's 900 s cap** (`timeout-minutes: 15`) — the step's "3 retries × 240 s" budget forgot the initial attempt. GitHub killed attempt 4 mid-flight; since the step never succeeds, the `actions/cache` save never warms, so both matrix arches fail every run.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (restore step only): retries moved to an explicit bash loop — 3 attempts × 240 s `--max-time` + 2 × 5 s sleeps = **730 s < 900 s**, leaving connect/unzip slack; each attempt resumes the partial zip with `-C -` (GitHub release assets serve Range requests). Verified empirically: curl's internal `--retry` restarts+truncates even with `-C -`, so the loop owns retries and curl owns resume.
- `rm -f /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip` before the loop so `-C -` only ever resumes this step's own partial bytes.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (new, static workflow lint) — RED before the fix (975 s worst case > 900 s, no `-C -`), now green: pins the budget arithmetic, single retry layer (no `curl --retry` under the loop), the `-C -` resume flag, and the fresh-seed rule.
